findings.title: No post-quantum key exchange
findings.detail: The server accepts no hybrid ML-KEM group. Key exchange is classical only (ECDHE or RSA), which a quantum computer will be able to break with Shor's algorithm: traffic captured today could be decrypted in the future ("harvest now, decrypt later"). This is the most urgent quantum risk because it affects data already in transit.
findings.remediation: Enable the hybrid group X25519MLKEM768 in TLS 1.3: OpenSSL 3.5+, BoringSSL, Go 1.24+, Caddy 2.10+, nginx built with OpenSSL 3.5, or your CDN or load balancer's post-quantum option. Keep X25519 as a fallback for older clients.

findings.title: DES cipher (56-bit) accepted
findings.detail: Single DES uses 56-bit keys, which have been brute-forced since 1998. Suites: TLS_RSA_WITH_DES_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_DES_CBC_SHA (SSLv3).
findings.remediation: Remove the DES suites (in OpenSSL, "!DES:!LOW") and use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

findings.title: EXPORT suites accepted
findings.detail: EXPORT suites use 40 or 56-bit keys, deliberately weakened in the 1990s by US export rules. Today they break in minutes and enable the FREAK (CVE-2015-0204) and Logjam (CVE-2015-4000) attacks. Suites: TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_RC4_40_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_RC2_CBC_40_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_DES40_CBC_SHA (SSLv3).
findings.remediation: Remove them (in OpenSSL, "!EXPORT") or upgrade the software: current releases no longer include them.

findings.title: Without TLS 1.3, hybrid ML-KEM key exchange cannot be adopted
findings.detail: The server only accepts versions older than TLS 1.3. That may be secure today, but hybrid ML-KEM groups only exist in TLS 1.3: until it is enabled, traffic stays exposed to "harvest now, decrypt later" and no group configuration can fix it.
findings.remediation: Enable TLS 1.3 (any server with OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later supports it, as do all current browsers), then the X25519MLKEM768 group. Keep TLS 1.2 for older clients.

findings.title: Small Diffie-Hellman group (1024 bits)
findings.detail: The DHE suites use a group under 2048 bits. The Logjam study (2015) estimated that a nation-state can break widely used 1024-bit groups; NIST requires 2048 bits or more.
findings.remediation: Configure a DH group of 2048 bits or more (ffdhe2048 or ffdhe3072, RFC 7919), or drop the DHE suites and keep ECDHE only.

findings.title: SSLv3 enabled
findings.detail: The server still accepts SSLv3, prohibited since 2015 (RFC 7568) because of the POODLE attack (CVE-2014-3566), which recovers encrypted data such as session cookies. No current browser uses it, so it only helps an attacker who forces that version.
findings.remediation: Disable SSLv3 (nginx: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; Apache: SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3).

findings.title: 3DES cipher accepted
findings.detail: 3DES uses 64-bit blocks and is vulnerable to Sweet32 on long connections. Suites: TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA (SSLv3).
findings.remediation: Remove the 3DES suites and use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

findings.title: RC4 cipher accepted
findings.detail: RC4 has exploitable statistical biases and is prohibited in TLS (RFC 7465). Suites: TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA (SSLv3).

findings.title: Suites without forward secrecy
findings.detail: Suites without an ephemeral key exchange, with RSA or static DH, are accepted (TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_RC4_40_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_RC4_128_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_RC2_CBC_40_MD5 (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_IDEA_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_EXPORT_WITH_DES40_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_DES_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_SEED_CBC_SHA (SSLv3)). Whoever obtains the server's private key could decrypt traffic captured with them.
findings.remediation: Remove the TLS_RSA_WITH_* suites and keep only ECDHE ones.

findings.title: Classical signature (RSA-2048): future quantum risk
findings.detail: The server proves its identity with RSA-2048, which a quantum computer will be able to forge. This is not "harvest now, decrypt later": a signature only has to hold during the handshake, so the risk starts the day such a computer exists, not before. It does not affect the grade.
findings.remediation: Nothing to do on the signature yet. Automate renewal (ACME) so you can switch to post-quantum (ML-DSA or hybrid) certificates as soon as authorities issue them: today this certificate shows no sign of renewing itself.

findings.title: No sign of automated renewal
findings.detail: 90-day validity, issued by QuantumReady TLS lab. Maximum certificate validity is already 200 days (since 15 March 2026) and will drop to 100 days on 15 March 2027 and to 47 on 15 March 2029 (CA/Browser Forum ballot SC-081). Moving to post-quantum certificates will require reissuing them: without automation, every change is manual work and an expiry risk.
findings.remediation: Automate issuance and renewal with ACME (certbot, Caddy, cert-manager…), with your current authority if it supports it or a free one.

findings.title: CBC-mode suites
findings.detail: TLS 1.2 CBC mode has suffered padding-oracle attacks (Lucky13 and the like) and depends on careful implementations. Suites: TLS_RSA_WITH_IDEA_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_CAMELLIA_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_RSA_WITH_SEED_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_SEED_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA (SSLv3), TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA (SSLv3).
findings.remediation: Prefer AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and remove CBC ones if your clients allow it.

findings.title: No transparency SCTs
findings.detail: No SCTs were found (neither embedded nor in the handshake). Browsers require them for public certificates, so this usually means a private certificate. Informational.

findings.title: Incomplete scan
findings.detail: 1 checks could not complete (timeout or network error). They were not counted as "not supported"; scan again to confirm them.

findings.title: Valid certificate
findings.detail: The chain is trusted, matches the name and is current (issuer: QuantumReady TLS lab; expires in 46 days).
